comment: Read at commit f50cb1b, the repository head. Two commits carry the installed 2.1.0: 2bb0b7c added the voice 3 Osc and Env outputs and f50cb1b added configInput and configOutput names for every jack. The installed build holds those names - Oscillator Pitch, Ring Mod Control Bit, Ext. SID Register Update Clock and the rest, which the census also lists - so f50cb1b is the build that shipped. The README says the pulse width CV reaches 0% at -1V and 100% at 1V; the code divides that voltage by 5, so the full sweep takes ±5V, and the lines say ±5V. Every jack is read with getVoltage() and no channel, and nothing calls setChannels or getPolyVoltage, so nothing here is polyphonic. The waveform, gate, sync, ring mod, test and filter switch inputs are added to the switch rather than overriding it, which means a negative voltage can switch off a control that is turned on; the README says only that 1V or more enables them. Ring modulation is masked off when the sawtooth is selected, from ring_msb_mask in resid/wave.cc:203; the sync and ring modulation sources are wired voice 1 from voice 3, voice 2 from voice 1 and voice 3 from voice 2 at resid/sid.cc:64-66. The SID register update rate, the lamps beside the CV jacks and the Clk output all move together: the lamps are written in the same block as the registers. The audio output scales a full-scale 16-bit sample to 20V, so no range is claimed for it. The ReSID sources under src/resid are Dag Lem's and were read only for the sync, ring modulation and test bit behaviour.
